Own scripted Playwright execution of the frozen golden (solve.sh install, sha256 of /app/server.js 72f3020b... and /app/public/assets/index.js fb2e3459... equal to the frozen files) in a throwaway container from local image cw-editor-verifier:current, headless Chromium 1440x900; container removed afterwards
counterexample: cw_focus_returns_to_code says 'Do the same check ... after clicking Save. Each time, the one character typed straight afterwards must be inserted into the source.' In the golden the Save button is disabled while the request is in flight (solution/app/src/app.tsx:152 'disabled: saveBusy') and focus is returned to the editor only in the finally block after the POST and the library refresh (app.tsx:75 'finally { setSaveBusy(false); editor.current?.focus(); }'). Measured gap between the Save click and focus arriving in the editor: 13-17 ms. A key pressed inside that gap goes to document.body and is dropped: with real input in one Playwright script (click Save, then keyboard.type('S') with no wait) the character was lost in 5 of 5 attempts, while the same character typed 700 ms later arrived. tests/app_context.md:19 explicitly allows real input through the Playwright code runner, so a judge that performs click and key press in one browser_run_code call would fail the golden on this criterion (one of six polish criteria, about 3.3% of the reward). A judge that issues the click and the key press as two separate tool calls is far slower than 17 ms and passes. Format, Undo, Redo and Replace all did not lose the character in the same tight script (0 of 5 for Format).
suggested_fix: In the golden's save(), move keyboard focus to the editor synchronously before awaiting the request (or do not disable the focused Save button while saving), so a key pressed directly after the Save click always lands in the source; then record a full configured Oracle judge run for the new candidate hash in the raw evidence index.
